scenarios.when: an alias resolves to multiple exact model IDs
scenarios.then: ask the user to choose an exact ID; do not submit

scenarios.when: the authenticated catalog lacks the exact image ID or capability
scenarios.then: state that the model is unavailable or unauthorized and list catalog candidates; do not submit

scenarios.when: the selected model has no authenticated live input schema for a requested n, size, image_size, aspect ratio, reference field, or other optional parameter
scenarios.then: explain that the model parameter profile is not published, ask the user to remove that option or choose a model with an explicit profile, and do not submit

scenarios.when: a requested optional parameter is absent from the authenticated live input schema or its value violates the declared enum or range
scenarios.then: list the profile-supported values and ask the user to choose one; do not submit

scenarios.when: the current connection cannot execute the request or deliver native image bytes
scenarios.then: stop before submission and ask the user to check the existing connection configuration

scenarios.when: the requested count is not allowed by the exact authenticated model's input_schema.properties.n
scenarios.then: explain the one-task limit, list the profile-declared count values or range, and ask for a supported count; do not submit

scenarios.when: a requested pixel canvas, semantic image size, aspect ratio, or other image parameter is not declared by the exact authenticated model profile
scenarios.then: list the profile-declared options for that field and ask the user to choose one; do not submit

scenarios.when: the request uses a physical dimension such as 200cm x 230cm
scenarios.then: explain that physical dimensions cannot be guaranteed and ask for a supported pixel canvas; do not submit

scenarios.when: the user attaches an image and the authenticated exact image model has no compatible input_schema.operations.image_edit profile
scenarios.then: state that this exact model has not published native image-attachment capability and do not submit or switch models

scenarios.when: the user provides a public reference-image URL but the exact authenticated profile lacks a matching property and declared public-URL reference transport
scenarios.then: state that the selected model has not published a compatible public-URL reference field, list any declared reference fields, and do not submit or switch models

scenarios.when: the user provides a reference-image URL that is not a public HTTPS URL
scenarios.then: explain that the selected profile requires a public HTTPS URL and ask the user to provide one; do not submit

scenarios.when: more than one exact authenticated public-URL reference field could represent the user's request
scenarios.then: list the declared fields and ask the user to choose the intended input mode; do not guess or submit

scenarios.when: an image-edit profile requires multipart_file but the current host cannot deliver the user's explicit attachment bytes through the configured connection
scenarios.then: stop before submission, explain that attachment-byte delivery is unavailable, and do not read credentials, create a URL, or downgrade to text-to-image

scenarios.when: the host can send the user's current multipart image attachment through the declared Images API operation
scenarios.then: send it only with that single Images API request; Pure Tokens stages the attachment internally to short-lived R2, waits for a readable public HTTPS URL, and never exposes that URL to the user

scenarios.when: an edit request includes a mask, multiple references, or another field not explicitly declared by the authenticated image_edit profile
scenarios.then: list the declared operation limits and ask the user to adjust the request; do not submit

scenarios.when: the same task is pending or running
scenarios.then: report the current state and continue reading only that task

scenarios.when: the same task is pending or running
scenarios.then: honor a valid positive Retry-After delay when returned; otherwise wait 3, 6, 12, 24, then 30 seconds, with at most six same-task status reads during a submission or explicit same-task continuation turn

scenarios.when: a task is pending or running
scenarios.then: keep at most one same-task status request in flight, never create a background timer or queue, and stop automatic polling after a rate limit, 5xx, transport error, or timeout

scenarios.when: 120 seconds have elapsed since a task submission response and the task is still pending or running
scenarios.then: report the current state, stop automatic polling, and require an explicit user request to continue the same task; do not resubmit

scenarios.when: the user explicitly asks to continue querying the returned task_id
scenarios.then: start a new bounded polling window for that same task only; do not submit, inspect, or substitute another task

scenarios.when: the same task reports failure, cancellation, or expiry
scenarios.then: report the returned failure and require an explicit new request before another submission

scenarios.when: the status request times out or the submission outcome is unknown
scenarios.then: report the uncertainty, offer to continue querying the same task if an ID exists, and never auto-resubmit

scenarios.when: a task is complete but native content cannot be delivered
scenarios.then: report the delivery failure and offer only a same-task content retry; do not claim success

scenarios.when: a multi-image task has delivered some but not every requested zero-based content index from 0 through n-1
scenarios.then: report the delivered and missing indexes, offer only same-task retrieval for the missing indexes, and never resubmit

scenarios.when: a completed task has multiple image results
scenarios.then: read zero-based content indexes sequentially, hand off each native byte result before the next read, and do not prefetch, concurrently fetch, or re-fetch delivered content
